item: GET /api/database/backup refuses a request from another site, writes its snapshot beside the database and takes one at a time
summary: The route wrote a full plaintext snapshot of the corpus into the operating system's temporary directory for any GET, so a page of another site could make the machine copy its corpus with one img tag. The refusal now lives in the route (not the middleware): Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin or none and Origin or Referer must name the request's own Host, the stricter of the two deciding; a caller that sends neither (curl, a script) is served. The snapshot goes in a .oo-backup-* folder (mode 0700) beside the database; a free-space gate compares the database plus its WAL with the volume (507 with both figures; an unreadable volume is not a refusal and the response carries X-OO-Free-Space-Check: not-read); one snapshot is made at a time (429); a FileResponse subclass removes the folder and frees the slot when the response ends or fails, a claim whose response never ran is taken over after 24 h, and a sweep removes only .oo-backup-* folders older than that (several servers per data folder stay safe, R176). An encrypted store is still refused (400). GET is kept. 21 tests: seven foreign-request forms refused before anything is written, own-page and non-browser callers served, location and mode, cleanup on failure and on response error, 507, 429, stale takeover, sweep, and an in-route source guard.
